  <!-- Mark library of the plain chart style (SPEC §4.5). Every symbol is drawn
       in a viewBox of -1…1 and placed with <use href="#mark-dot" x y width
       height>: the layout gives the size, the stylesheet the colour (the
       symbols inherit fill and stroke from the <use>). Black-and-white
       symbols (R6-30) are for later stages. -->

    <symbol id="mark-dot" viewBox="-1 -1 2 2" overflow="visible"><circle r="1"/></symbol>
    <symbol id="mark-square" viewBox="-1 -1 2 2" overflow="visible"><rect x="-0.886" y="-0.886" width="1.772" height="1.772"/></symbol>

    <symbol id="mark-plus" viewBox="-1 -1 2 2" overflow="visible"><path d="M0,-1 L0,1 M-1,0 L1,0" fill="none" stroke-width="0.35"/></symbol>

    <!-- phase 2: the highlight icon (R15-5, s. 0370), a small marker pointing at its target -->
    <symbol id="mark-icon-down" viewBox="-1 -1 2 2" overflow="visible"><path d="M-0.75,-1 L0.75,-1 L0.75,0.15 L0,1 L-0.75,0.15 z"/></symbol>
    <symbol id="mark-icon-up" viewBox="-1 -1 2 2" overflow="visible"><path d="M-0.75,1 L0.75,1 L0.75,-0.15 L0,-1 L-0.75,-0.15 z"/></symbol>
    <symbol id="mark-icon-left" viewBox="-1 -1 2 2" overflow="visible"><path d="M1,-0.75 L1,0.75 L-0.15,0.75 L-1,0 L-0.15,-0.75 z"/></symbol>
    <symbol id="mark-icon-right" viewBox="-1 -1 2 2" overflow="visible"><path d="M-1,-0.75 L-1,0.75 L0.15,0.75 L1,0 L0.15,-0.75 z"/></symbol>
    <!-- (phase 2: comments' arrows carry the house arrowhead, bent along the curve, drawn as

/* The plain chart style without its data colours (SPEC §5): the book's plain
   look, flat on the page, labels in New Computer Modern at 10 pt (owner,
   30 Sep 2026), titles 1.2 times and bold. Values are tokens on :root; the
   role rules below use them through var(). chartgen flattens this file
   (imports inlined, em in points, var() replaced) before bake.py reads it.

   Order matters (bake.py takes, for each class of a label, the first rule
   that mentions it): tokens, text roles (.prose first, then single-class
   rules), non-data, slot paints, highlight and context paints, then the
   mark-kind rules, which reset what does not apply to a kind.

   Tagged M (measured in the book), N (the notes' proposal), O (ours). An em
   is --label-size, never a CSS em. */
/* @defs plain-defs.svg */

:root {
  /* typography */
  --label-size: 10;                /* owner: the diagrams' size, at the 368 pt text width */
  --title-size: 1.2em;             /* M 1.17–1.35; bold */
  --note-size: 0.8em;              /* M; italic; the floor of D-6 */
  --inset-text-size: 0.8em;        /* M 0.73–0.82 */
  --line-pitch: 1.25em;            /* M 1.25–1.3: wrapped labels, title lines */
  --text-pad: 0.15em;              /* O: padding of text boxes in the collision test */

  /* notes under the chart and their marks (SPEC §6.19; owner, 1 Oct 2026: tables and charts may carry
     footnotes); the marks' look is the owner's to choose, the alternatives in examples/review/r1-footnotes */
  --note-marks: letters;           /* O: the marks' sequence, numbered in reading order: letters (a, b, c),
                                      numerals (1, 2, 3) or symbols (*, †, ‡, §, ‖, ¶); letters, since a raised
                                      figure beside a number can read as an exponent */
  --note-mark-gap: 0.05em;         /* O: a mark's gap after the text it marks (the face's side bearing does most) */
  --note-mark-lift: 0;             /* O: a mark's x-height (letters, numerals; figure height for symbols) at the
                                      cap height of the text it marks, then raised this much more */
  --note-hang: 0.3em;              /* O: a note's mark to its text under the chart; its later lines indented to the
                                      text */
  --note-mark-size: var(--note-size);  /* O: the notes' size, 0.8em, the floor of G6.4 */
  --note-mark-slant: italic;       /* O: italic, as the notes (README: the chart's own notes are italic) */
  --note-mark-ink: var(--note);    /* O: the note grey (4.5 : 1); on a fill, the colour of the text it marks */
  --note-footer-marks: raised;     /* O: a note's own mark under the chart, raised as in the chart, or on the
                                      baseline (baseline) */
  --notes-gap: 1em;                /* O: the chart's lowest ink to the first note's cap tops */

  /* value scale and unit phrase (6.4) */
  --scale-gap: 0.9em;              /* M 0.9–1.0: label column's right edge to the plot */
  --unit-space: 0.333em;           /* O: the typeface's word space, number to phrase */
  --unit-gridline-gap: 0.6em;      /* M 0.5–0.7: phrase end to the top gridline's start */
  --unit-min-gridline: 0.15;       /* N: shortest top gridline, a share of the plot width */
  --unit-clearance: 0.3em;         /* N: padding of the phrase in the collision test */
  --scale-label-drop: 0.5em;       /* M: horizontal scale, plot bottom to the labels' cap tops */
  --unit-line-drop: 0.55em;        /* O: horizontal scale, label row to the unit line's cap top (a line pitch
                                      between baselines; M 0.3 looked cramped at 10 pt) */

  /* categories and time (6.3, 6.7) */
  --category-gap: 0.8em;           /* M 0.6–1.0: zero line to the cap tops of category labels */
  --category-label-gap: 0.6em;     /* M: horizontal bars, label right edge to the plot */
  --category-label-sep: 1em;       /* owner (30 Sep 2026): least clear space between neighbouring names
                                      under vertical bars, which may reach past their bands; the gap must
                                      read wider than the spaces inside a name */
  --time-row-pitch: 1.8em;         /* M ≈ 2: cap top to cap top between time rows */
  --time-label-sep: 0.6em;         /* N: thinning, least space between time labels */
  --divider-clear: 0.3em;          /* O (owner, 30 Sep 2026): least space between a time label and a
                                      divider, half the space between two labels; the outer dividers move
                                      out to keep it, a label beside an inner one keeps its place with a halo */
  --divider-halo: 0.6em;           /* O (owner, 1 Oct 2026): the halo's stroke round a label's letters, twice
                                      --divider-clear, so that it reaches the clearance outside them */

  /* title block (D-5: left-aligned, a descriptive line in the label style) */
  --title-gap: 1.6em;              /* O: last title baseline to the top scale line's baseline */
  --title-align: start;            /* D-5 (a): left, flush with the scale labels */
  --title-align-insight: start;

  /* plot and bars */
  --plot-aspect: 0.6;              /* M ≈ 0.64; O: plot height / plot width */
  --bar-row-pitch: 2em;            /* O: band of horizontal bars when the height is free */
  --band-fill: 0.556;              /* M 0.55–0.56: bar : gap = 5 : 4 (R9-8, D-35) */
  --cluster-fill: 0.714;           /* M 0.72 (phase 2) */
  --cluster-inner-gap: 0;          /* M: bars of a cluster touch */
  --cluster-min-gap: 1;            /* G7.5s: clusters at least one bar width apart (M 1.0 with 2–3 series, s. 0307,
                                      0319; 2.25 with six, s. 0331: the cluster fill gives 2.4) (phase 2) */
  --target-mark: 0.2;              /* G7.57s: a flat reference marker's thickness, in bar widths (M s. 0321) */
  --target-mark-max: 0.4em;        /* M ≈ 0.36–0.4em (s. 0148, s. 0321): no thicker, however wide the bars */
  --value-label-gap: 0.3em;        /* O: a value label's gap to its bar's end (G7.4) (phase 2) */
  --table-gap: 2em;                /* M ≈ 2em (s. 0307): the last category row's baseline to a companion
                                      table's first row (phase 2) */
  --table-row-pitch: 1.6em;        /* M ≈ 1.65em (s. 0307): a companion table's rows (G7.39s gives 2.15em for
                                      a table alone) */
  --table-col-gap: 1.5em;          /* G7.39s: between a table's columns, and between the bars and a table beside
                                      them */
  --table-header-drop: 0.75em;     /* O: a table beside horizontal bars, its headers' baseline above the plot */
  --key-gap: 0.25em;               /* O: a table row's key square to its name (the legend's --legend-gap) */
  --key-tint: 0.6;                 /* O: a row's pill or halo, its series colour this far towards the page (the
                                      least at which the text grey keeps 4.5 : 1 on all of slots 1-3: 4.68 on the
                                      orange) */
  --key-pill-pad-x: 0.35em;        /* O: a pill's room either side of its name */
  --key-pill-pad-y: 0.2em;         /* O: and above and below the name's capitals (plus 1 pt) */
  --key-halo-width: 0.3em;         /* O: a halo's stroke round the letters (half of it shows outside them) */
  --missing-note-lift: 0.3em;      /* O: note baseline above the zero line */
  --missing-note-inset: 0.3em;     /* O: horizontal bars, zero line to the note */

  /* lines, dots and end labels (later stages) */
  --line-width: 0.2em;             /* M 0.15–0.23em */
  --line-width-highlight: 0.4em;   /* M × 2 (06) */
  --marker-size: 0.4em;            /* M: diameter, twice the line */
  --dot-size: 0.5em;               /* M: a time dot plot's filled dot (s. 0163) */
  --category-dot-size: 0.75em;     /* M: a categorical dot plot's open circle, centre-line diameter (outside
                                      ≈ 0.85em with its ring; s. 0082, 0085) */
  --dot-ring: 0.3;                 /* M: the open circle's ring in units of its radius (≈ 1.1 pt; s. 0085) */
  --end-label-gap: 0.5em;          /* M 0.3–0.9 */
  --end-label-pitch: 1.25em;       /* M */
  --end-label-max-shift: 1;        /* N: pitches, then a legend */
  --end-label-leader-shift: 1.5;   /* D-7: pitches a label may move with a leader to its line */
  --leader-run: 1em;               /* O: how much further right a label with a leader sits */
  --legend-margin: 1em;            /* O: plot edge to a legend column at its right (lines) */

  /* time charts of phase 2: thin bars, true time axes, arrows, symbols */
  --event-bar-width: 0.28em;       /* D-42: a thin bar 1.2–1.5 × the line width (1.4 ×); M ≈ 1.2–1.5 × (s. 0181) */
  --time-tick: 0.45em;             /* D-45 (ii): a true time axis's tick at a boundary of its labelled unit */
  --time-tick-minor: 0.25em;       /* D-45 (ii): a tick at each day (or month) of the data's grain */
  --arrow-head-length: 0.65em;     /* notes 06 §5.4: about 3 × the line width; the tip on the after value */
  --arrow-head-width: 0.55em;      /* about 2.5 × the line width */
  --arrow-start-size: 0.5em;       /* the dot at the before value, about 2.2 × the line width (diameter) */
  --arrow-panel-gap: 2em;          /* O: between an arrow chart's absolute and % panels */
  --arrow-short-head: fit;         /* O (owner to judge, review r1-arrows): a change shorter than a full head
                                      beside its dot: fit (the head shrinks to the room, to half size, then
                                      overhangs the dot, haloed), overhang, head-only, or hidden (the former) */
  --arrow-head-halo: 0.12em;       /* O: the page-coloured outline round a head drawn over its start dot */
  --symbol-size: 0.55em;           /* R6-30: a black-and-white marker symbol, M ≈ 0.5em (s. 0200) */

  /* insets (6.6) */
  --inset-frame-width: 1.5;        /* M 2.5–4 × the gridline: frames and links */
  --inset-radius: 6;               /* M ≈ 1.8 % of the chart width */
  --inset-pad-x: 0.3;              /* N: bands, source frame round its marks, across them */
  --inset-pad-y: 0.4em;            /* N: source frame round its marks, along them; round a band */
  --inset-margin: 0.6em;           /* O: frame to inset content; a band's source frame inside the inset's */
  --inset-gap: 1.5em;              /* O: between a band inset's frame and its source frame, where the links run
                                      (M ≈ 1.6em, s. 0081, s. 0297) */
  --inset-fade: 0.85;              /* M: bar widths faded below the lowest inset gridline (s. 0297) */
  --inset-height-ratio: 0.8;       /* M: narrow-range inset plot / main plot */
  --inset-max-height: 1;           /* owner (30 Sep 2026): an inset's plot at most about as high as its main
                                      chart's (above or below it) */
  --inset-share-height: 0.9;       /* O: an aligned inset shares its main chart's axis when, labelled twice,
                                      the figure would be taller than this × its width (D-56) */

  /* small multiples and merged charts (phase 2, 6.10) */
  --panel-gap: 0.8em;              /* O: least space between the texts of neighbouring panels (merged bars:
                                      M about one band, notes 02 §5.3); a separator runs in its middle */
  --panel-min-height: 3em;         /* O: a panel's plot at least this high, three intervals one em apart, so
                                      that a stack of twelve fits a page (the book's stacks ≈ 3.5–4em, s. 0203) */
  --panel-max-aspect: 1.5;         /* O: a panel's plot at most this × its width high (the book's rows of
                                      panels, s. 0339–0340, stand 1.5–1.8 × as high as wide) */

  /* legends (phase 2) */
  --legend-key: 0.55em;            /* M: square key; a line key is 2em */
  --legend-line-key: 2em;
  --legend-gap: 0.25em;            /* M: key to text */
  --legend-entry-gap: 1em;         /* M: between entries */

  /* one total's breakdown (phase 3): pies, treemaps, wrapped bars */
  --pie-radius: 0.2;               /* O: the pie's radius, a share of the figure's width (M ≈ 0.18-0.19 of the
                                      book's column, s. 0265), smaller when its labels need the room */
  --pie-min-radius: 3em;           /* O: no smaller; a pie whose labels will not fit round it then is refused */
  --pie-gap: 0.007;                /* G7.26s, M: the gap between slices, a share of the diameter (a true gap:
                                      each slice's straight edges moved in by half of it) */
  --pie-label-gap: 0.1;            /* N (07 §5.2): the rim to a label's nearest point, a share of the radius */
  --pie-label-width: 7em;          /* O: a slice's name wider than this wraps onto two lines (s. 0222) */
  --pie-leader-angle: 8;           /* D-34, N: a slice under this many degrees gets a leader (G7.29) */
  --donut-hole: 0.74;              /* M (s. 0269): a donut's hole, a share of its radius (only through an
                                      override of R7-39) */
  --tile-gap: 1;                   /* M 1 px: the page between neighbouring tiles of a treemap (G7.34) */
  --tile-group-gap: 2.5;           /* M 1-2 px at the book's size: between the groups of a treemap */
  --tile-pad: 0.3em;               /* M ≈ 3 px: a tile's label inset from its lower left corner */
  --tile-min-chars: 3;             /* O: a name cut short keeps at least this many letters before "…" */
  --wrap-max-aspect: 1.2;          /* O: a wrapped bar chart's columns at most this × the figure's width high;
                                      the fewest columns that keep within it (G7.7) */
  --wrap-column-gap: 1.5em;        /* O: between a column's scale labels and the next column's names */

  /* greys and lines (5.3) */
  --grid-width: 0.6;               /* O: the diagrams' hairline (M ≈ 0.72 at this size) */
  --page: #ffffff;
  --text: #595959;                 /* M; contrast 7.0 */
  --note: #767676;                 /* O: 4.5 : 1 (D-6), not the book's ≈ #B0B0B0 */
  --grid: #d9d9d9;                 /* M; contrast 1.41 */
  --zero-line: #d9d9d9;            /* M: the zero line is a gridline (R1-07) */
  --zero-line-signed: #a6a6a6;     /* M: darker only inside a signed range (D-17) */
  --divider: #d9d9d9;
  --inset-frame: #d9d9d9;
  --projection-dash: 0 5;          /* M: dots one line wide */
  --projection-dash-highlight: 0 10;  /* O: the same dots on a line twice as thick */
  --leader: #bfbfbf;               /* M: the book's leader grey (pie leaders #C0C0C0, 5.5) */
  --uniform-context: #bfbfbf;      /* M: only for rebuilding the rejected grey-out (R6-28) */
  --comment: #3f63b0;              /* N (phase 2) */
  --link: #bfbfbf;                 /* M (phase 2) */
  --tile-text: #1a1a1a;            /* O (phase 3): a treemap tile's label, at least 4.5 : 1 on every first-tier
                                      colour and the sixth (4.7 on the purple; the text grey is 3.3 on the blue,
                                      and the book's white on its #558BB9 is 3.6) */
}

/* ---- Text. Every label is <text class="prose modifiers… role">. ---------- */
.prose        { font-family: NewComputerModern, "New Computer Modern"; font-size: var(--label-size);
                fill: var(--text); }
.title        { font-size: var(--title-size); font-weight: bold; }
.missing-note { font-size: var(--note-size); font-style: italic; fill: var(--note); }
.incomplete-note { font-size: var(--note-size); font-style: italic; fill: var(--note); }  /* "As of Dec. 10" */
.arrow-key    { font-size: var(--note-size); fill: var(--note); }  /* G7.21s: the arrow key; upright, italic is the comments' (owner, 30 Sep 2026) */
.inset-text   { font-size: var(--inset-text-size); }
.text-strong  { font-weight: bold; }
.panel-title  { font-weight: bold; }   /* a merged chart's panel heading (G7.6: bold, M s. 0067, 0363) */
.tile-label   { fill: var(--tile-text); }   /* a treemap's names, inside their tiles (phase 3) */
.chart-note   { font-size: var(--note-size); font-style: italic; fill: var(--note); }  /* the chart's own note
                                                 under it: a treemap's parts too small to name (phase 3) */
.footnote     { font-size: var(--note-size); font-style: italic; fill: var(--note); }  /* a note under the chart
                                                 referred to by its mark (SPEC §6.19); a plain note is a chart-note */
.note-mark    { font-size: var(--note-mark-size); font-style: var(--note-mark-slant); fill: var(--note-mark-ink); }
                                              /* a note's mark, raised,
                                                 after what it explains and before the note (SPEC §6.19) */
.on-fill      { fill: var(--text); }   /* a note's mark on a filled cell or tile, after the classes of the text it
                                          marks: in that text's colour, never the note grey (SPEC §6.19) */

/* ---- Non-data: light and thin, under the marks (R1-02, R1-09). ------------ */
.gridline             { fill: none; stroke: var(--grid); stroke-width: var(--grid-width); }
.gridline.zero        { stroke: var(--zero-line); }
.gridline.zero.signed { stroke: var(--zero-line-signed); }
.time-divider         { fill: none; stroke: var(--divider); stroke-width: var(--grid-width); }
.panel-divider        { fill: none; stroke: var(--divider); stroke-width: var(--grid-width); }  /* G7.51 */
.inset-frame         { fill: var(--page); stroke: var(--inset-frame); stroke-width: var(--inset-frame-width); }
.inset-source, .inset-link { fill: none; stroke: var(--inset-frame); stroke-width: var(--inset-frame-width); }

/* ---- Data colours by slot or role (tokens in the palette file). ------------ */
.single     { fill: var(--single); stroke: var(--single); }
.series-1   { fill: var(--series-1); stroke: var(--series-1); }
.series-2   { fill: var(--series-2); stroke: var(--series-2); }
.series-3   { fill: var(--series-3); stroke: var(--series-3); }
.series-4   { fill: var(--series-4); stroke: var(--series-4); }
.series-5   { fill: var(--series-5); stroke: var(--series-5); }
.series-6   { fill: var(--series-6); stroke: var(--series-6); }
.series-7   { fill: var(--series-7); stroke: var(--series-7); }
.series-8   { fill: var(--series-8); stroke: var(--series-8); }
.series-9   { fill: var(--series-9); stroke: var(--series-9); }
.series-10  { fill: var(--series-10); stroke: var(--series-10); }
.series-11  { fill: var(--series-11); stroke: var(--series-11); }
.series-12  { fill: var(--series-12); stroke: var(--series-12); }
.series-13  { fill: var(--series-13); stroke: var(--series-13); }
.series-14  { fill: var(--series-14); stroke: var(--series-14); }
.series-15  { fill: var(--series-15); stroke: var(--series-15); }
.series-16  { fill: var(--series-16); stroke: var(--series-16); }
.average    { fill: var(--average); stroke: var(--average); }
.total      { fill: var(--total); stroke: var(--total); }
.all-others { fill: var(--all-others); stroke: var(--all-others); }
.reference  { fill: var(--reference-line); stroke: var(--reference-line); }
.missing    { fill: var(--missing); stroke: var(--missing); }
.good       { fill: var(--good); stroke: var(--good); }
.bad        { fill: var(--bad); stroke: var(--bad); }

/* ---- Highlight: the same hue, stronger (R3-7, R15-6, 6.9). ----------------- */
.single.highlight     { fill: var(--single-strong); stroke: var(--single-strong); }
.series-1.highlight   { fill: var(--series-1-strong); stroke: var(--series-1-strong); }
.series-2.highlight   { fill: var(--series-2-strong); stroke: var(--series-2-strong); }
.series-3.highlight   { fill: var(--series-3-strong); stroke: var(--series-3-strong); }
.series-4.highlight   { fill: var(--series-4-strong); stroke: var(--series-4-strong); }
.series-5.highlight   { fill: var(--series-5-strong); stroke: var(--series-5-strong); }
.series-6.highlight   { fill: var(--series-6-strong); stroke: var(--series-6-strong); }
.series-7.highlight   { fill: var(--series-7-strong); stroke: var(--series-7-strong); }
.series-8.highlight   { fill: var(--series-8-strong); stroke: var(--series-8-strong); }
.series-9.highlight   { fill: var(--series-9-strong); stroke: var(--series-9-strong); }
.series-10.highlight  { fill: var(--series-10-strong); stroke: var(--series-10-strong); }
.series-11.highlight  { fill: var(--series-11-strong); stroke: var(--series-11-strong); }
.series-12.highlight  { fill: var(--series-12-strong); stroke: var(--series-12-strong); }
.series-13.highlight  { fill: var(--series-13-strong); stroke: var(--series-13-strong); }
.series-14.highlight  { fill: var(--series-14-strong); stroke: var(--series-14-strong); }
.series-15.highlight  { fill: var(--series-15-strong); stroke: var(--series-15-strong); }
.series-16.highlight  { fill: var(--series-16-strong); stroke: var(--series-16-strong); }

/* Context (dim_others, bars only, 07 §5.1): the colour paled towards the page. */
.single.context       { fill: var(--single-context); stroke: var(--single-context); }
.series-1.context     { fill: var(--series-1-context); stroke: var(--series-1-context); }
.series-2.context     { fill: var(--series-2-context); stroke: var(--series-2-context); }
.series-3.context     { fill: var(--series-3-context); stroke: var(--series-3-context); }
.series-4.context     { fill: var(--series-4-context); stroke: var(--series-4-context); }
.series-5.context     { fill: var(--series-5-context); stroke: var(--series-5-context); }
.series-6.context     { fill: var(--series-6-context); stroke: var(--series-6-context); }

/* Tint (phase 3): the second part of a group in a pie, its group's colour paled towards the page
   (07 #10, s. 0240: Sports cars in the blue, Other cars in its tint). */
.series-1.tint        { fill: var(--series-1-tint); stroke: var(--series-1-tint); }
.series-2.tint        { fill: var(--series-2-tint); stroke: var(--series-2-tint); }
.series-3.tint        { fill: var(--series-3-tint); stroke: var(--series-3-tint); }

.series-6.tint        { fill: var(--series-6-tint); stroke: var(--series-6-tint); }

/* Lines take their own single colour (R3-3; 00-01 F5). */
.line.single, .projection.single                   { stroke: var(--single-line); }
.line.single.highlight, .projection.single.highlight { stroke: var(--single-line-strong); }

/* Line charts (stage 2). A single line's markers take its colour; reference series are in
   the reserved dark grey (R6-34, D-21 (c)): an average or total solid, a target or outside
   benchmark dotted (the layout draws it as a projection, classed reference). Leaders and
   legend keys. */
.point.single, .legend-key.single              { fill: var(--single-line); stroke: var(--single-line); }
.point.single.highlight, .legend-key.single.highlight { fill: var(--single-line-strong); stroke: var(--single-line-strong); }
.line.total, .projection.total, .point.total, .legend-key.total { fill: var(--average); stroke: var(--average); }
.line.reference, .projection.reference, .point.reference,
.legend-key.reference                           { fill: var(--average); stroke: var(--average); }
.chart .projection.highlight { stroke-dasharray: var(--projection-dash-highlight); }
.leader       { fill: none; stroke: var(--leader); stroke-width: var(--grid-width); }
.legend-key   { fill: none; stroke-width: var(--line-width); stroke-linecap: round; }
.legend-key.highlight { stroke-width: var(--line-width-highlight); }

/* ---- Mark kinds: flat, no outlines (R1-03). --------------------------------- */
.chart .bar   { stroke: none; }
.chart .line, .chart .projection { fill: none; stroke-width: var(--line-width);
                stroke-linejoin: round; stroke-linecap: round; }
.chart .line.highlight, .chart .projection.highlight { stroke-width: var(--line-width-highlight); }
.chart .projection { stroke-dasharray: var(--projection-dash); }
.chart .point, .chart .dot { stroke-width: 0; }
.chart.categorical .dot { fill: none; stroke-width: var(--dot-ring); }  /* hollow (s. 0085); symbol units */
.uniform-context { fill: var(--uniform-context); stroke: var(--uniform-context); }  /* rejected grey-out only */

/* Time charts of phase 2. A step line keeps square corners and stops exactly at the as-of
   date (notes 06 §5.4); a thin bar is flat like a bar; a true time axis has short ticks in the
   divider grey (D-45 (ii)); an arrow's shaft is a line, its head and start dot filled; the
   level mark of an incomplete period is dotted like a projection (02 D10). */
.step-line.single, .incomplete-mark.single       { stroke: var(--single-line); }
.chart .step-line   { fill: none; stroke-width: var(--line-width); stroke-linejoin: miter; stroke-linecap: butt; }
.chart .event-bar   { stroke: none; }
.time-tick          { fill: none; stroke: var(--divider); stroke-width: var(--grid-width); }
.chart .change-shaft { fill: none; stroke-width: var(--line-width); stroke-linecap: butt; }
.chart .change-head, .chart .change-start { stroke-width: 0; }
.chart .arrow-halo  { fill: var(--page); stroke: var(--page); stroke-width: var(--arrow-head-halo);
                      stroke-linejoin: round; }   /* a short change's head over its start dot */
.chart .incomplete-mark { fill: none; stroke-width: var(--line-width); stroke-dasharray: var(--projection-dash);
                          stroke-linecap: round; }
/* A time label beside a divider (owner, 1 Oct 2026): a knock-out halo, a copy of its letters
   (text-halo) filled and stroked in the page colour under it, so that the divider stops short of
   the letters by the clearance instead of crossing them (flat: no card, no shadow). */
.divider-halo use { fill: var(--page); stroke: var(--page); stroke-width: var(--divider-halo);
                    stroke-linejoin: round; }

/* Several series over categories (phase 2). A bar's legend key is a small filled square, a
   dot's the dot itself, open or filled as the chart's dots are (G5.14); a flat reference
   marker across a bar, and its key, in the strong shade of the bar's hue (R11-4, G7.57), else
   in the reserved dark grey. */
.legend-swatch  { stroke: none; }
.chart .dot-key { stroke-width: 0; }
.chart.categorical .dot-key { fill: none; stroke-width: var(--dot-ring); }
.chart .target-mark, .target-key          { fill: var(--average); stroke: none; }
.target-mark.single, .target-key.single     { fill: var(--single-strong); }
.target-mark.series-1, .target-key.series-1 { fill: var(--series-1-strong); }
.target-mark.series-2, .target-key.series-2 { fill: var(--series-2-strong); }
.target-mark.series-3, .target-key.series-3 { fill: var(--series-3-strong); }
.target-mark.series-4, .target-key.series-4 { fill: var(--series-4-strong); }
.target-mark.series-5, .target-key.series-5 { fill: var(--series-5-strong); }
.target-mark.series-6, .target-key.series-6 { fill: var(--series-6-strong); }

/* A table's row keys (table.row_key; phase 2, for the owner's choice): a name in its series'
   strong shade (text-*), a pale tint of the series behind the name (a pill) or round its letters
   (a flat halo: a copy of the name, text-halo, filled and stroked in the tint under the name). */
.text-single    { fill: var(--single-strong); }
.text-series-1  { fill: var(--series-1-strong); }
.text-series-2  { fill: var(--series-2-strong); }
.text-series-3  { fill: var(--series-3-strong); }
.text-series-4  { fill: var(--series-4-strong); }
.text-series-5  { fill: var(--series-5-strong); }
.text-series-6  { fill: var(--series-6-strong); }
.text-halo      { }
.key-pill       { stroke: none; }
.key-pill.single, .key-halo.single use     { fill: mix(var(--single), #ffffff, var(--key-tint)); }
.key-pill.series-1, .key-halo.series-1 use { fill: mix(var(--series-1), #ffffff, var(--key-tint)); }
.key-pill.series-2, .key-halo.series-2 use { fill: mix(var(--series-2), #ffffff, var(--key-tint)); }
.key-pill.series-3, .key-halo.series-3 use { fill: mix(var(--series-3), #ffffff, var(--key-tint)); }
.key-pill.series-4, .key-halo.series-4 use { fill: mix(var(--series-4), #ffffff, var(--key-tint)); }
.key-pill.series-5, .key-halo.series-5 use { fill: mix(var(--series-5), #ffffff, var(--key-tint)); }
.key-pill.series-6, .key-halo.series-6 use { fill: mix(var(--series-6), #ffffff, var(--key-tint)); }
.key-halo.single use     { stroke: mix(var(--single), #ffffff, var(--key-tint)); }
.key-halo.series-1 use   { stroke: mix(var(--series-1), #ffffff, var(--key-tint)); }
.key-halo.series-2 use   { stroke: mix(var(--series-2), #ffffff, var(--key-tint)); }
.key-halo.series-3 use   { stroke: mix(var(--series-3), #ffffff, var(--key-tint)); }
.key-halo.series-4 use   { stroke: mix(var(--series-4), #ffffff, var(--key-tint)); }
.key-halo.series-5 use   { stroke: mix(var(--series-5), #ffffff, var(--key-tint)); }
.key-halo.series-6 use   { stroke: mix(var(--series-6), #ffffff, var(--key-tint)); }
.key-halo use            { stroke-width: var(--key-halo-width); stroke-linejoin: round; }

/* One total's breakdown (phase 3): a pie's slices and a treemap's tiles are flat, with no outline
   (R7-33, G7.26: the page shows between them through true gaps); a leader to a small or zero slice
   is a thin grey curve with the house arrowhead (R7-37, s. 0266). */
.chart .slice, .chart .tile { stroke: none; }
.leader-head  { fill: var(--leader); stroke: none; }

/* ---- Tables alone, heatmaps, ramps and their keys (phase 3; SPEC §6.14–§6.16). ------------ */
:root {
  /* a table alone (R10-12–R10-25; G7.37–G7.45; D-52) */
  --table-alone-pitch: 2.15em;     /* G7.39s, M ≈ 2.15em (s. 0315): rows set well apart, no stripes */
  --table-total-gap: 3em;          /* G7.39s, M ≈ 3em: the gutter before a Total column (1.5em elsewhere,
                                      --table-col-gap) */
  --table-rule-width: 0.6;         /* M 1 px: the rule under the header and the one above the totals */
  --table-rule-drop: 0.6em;        /* O: the header's baseline to its rule */
  --table-fill-pad: 0.35em;        /* O: a highlighted cell's fill beyond its text, each side (M s. 0317) */
  --table-fill-inset: 0.2em;       /* O: a fill's top and bottom inside its row's pitch (M ≈ 1.8 of 2.15em) */
  --table-rule: #a3a3a3;           /* M s. 0317 (D-52 (iii)): under the header, mid grey */
  --table-rule-total: #656565;     /* M s. 0317: above the totals, darker */
  --table-fill: #e8e8e8;           /* G7.44s, M s. 0317: the few cells that matter */
  /* heatmaps (R6-36, R12-6; G7.35, G7.36) */
  --cell-pitch: 1.6em;             /* M ≈ 1.7em (s. 0329, s. 0309): the rows of a heatmap table or a shaded
                                      table; the cells touch */
  --heat-row-pitch: 1em;           /* O: a heatmap of many series, a row each: its names at the label size (the
                                      layout widens it when names with descenders would meet; the book's names
                                      are tiny, s. 0204) */
  --summary-gap: 0.4em;            /* M ≈ 0.3 row (s. 0329): a summary row (Overall Avg.) set apart */
  --heat-max-column: 5em;          /* O: a heatmap table's columns at most this wide (cells of the widest value
                                      and heading otherwise) */
  /* a ramp's key (G5.13, R4-9): a graduated bar, its title above, its values below */
  --ramp-key-width: 12em;          /* O (M ≈ 14em × 1.3em at the book's size, 03-04 §5.4) */
  --ramp-key-height: 0.7em;
  --ramp-key-gap: 0.35em;          /* O: the title to the bar, the bar to its values */
  --key-tick: 0.3em;               /* O: the mark at a diverging key's dividing value */
  /* in-table graphics (R10-9, G7.47) */
  --cell-bar-height: 0.9em;        /* O: a bar under its cell's number (M ≈ 0.6 of the row, s. 0309) */
  --cell-dot: 0.55em;              /* O: a dot in its cell's strip */
  --cell-strip: 3em;               /* O: the strip of dots beside a column's numbers */
  --sparkline-width: 0.12em;       /* M ≈ 1.5 px (s. 0309) */
  --trend-width: 4em;              /* O: the Trend column's sparklines */
  /* action dots (R12-4, G7.58) */
  --action-pitch: 2em;             /* M ≈ 2.3em (s. 0327) */
  --action-bar: 0.35;              /* M: the bar's thickness, a share of the row's pitch */
  --action-bar-length: 8em;        /* O: the longest bar */
  --action-dot: 0.75em;            /* M ≈ 0.9 × the text's height (s. 0327) */
  --action-gap: 0.6em;             /* O: between the name, the bar, the value and the dot */
  /* values printed in strong cells (owner, 1 Oct 2026; a muted cell, chart.cells, is the spec's):
     contrast (the owner's choice: each value black or white, whichever has more contrast on its
     cell) or plate (the value in the text grey on a plate of the step's pale version, kept for
     comparison); ramps.CELL_VALUE_MODES */
  --cell-values: contrast;
  --cell-text-dark: #000000;       /* O: on a mid cell only black keeps 4.5 : 1 (4.68 on --seq-7; #1a1a1a 3.88) */
  --cell-text-light: #ffffff;
  --cell-plate-pad: 0.2em;         /* O: a plate's margin round a value's ink */
  /* censored values in a heatmap ("<1" below a detection limit, ">2,420" above a range; SPEC §6.15), a
     state of their own, never the missing grey: step (a step of the ramp of their own below its lowest
     class, its own entry in the key), printed (the palest class's colour, "<1" printed in the cell),
     pale (a pale fill of their own), hatch or dots (the page under a fine hatch or dots). The owner's
     choice to make (examples/review/r1-below-limit); step provisionally. */
  --censored-cells: step;
  --censored: #e4e0da;             /* O: pale, lighter than the missing grey (#a6a6a6), apart from the page */
  --censored-mark: #8c8c8c;        /* O: the hatch's lines and the dots, on the page's white */
  --censored-hatch-gap: 0.25em;
  --censored-dot: 0.09em;
}
.chart .censored, .legend-swatch.censored { fill: var(--censored); stroke: none; }
.chart .censored-hatched, .chart .censored-dotted, .legend-swatch.censored-hatched,
.legend-swatch.censored-dotted { fill: var(--page); stroke: none; }
.censored-hatch { fill: none; stroke: var(--censored-mark); stroke-width: 0.45; }
.censored-dot   { fill: var(--censored-mark); stroke: none; }
/* A table alone: two thin rules and space, no grid, no stripes, nothing bold but the title
   (G7.38–G7.43); the few cells that matter on a light fill (G7.44); stripes only through an
   override (R10-16), to rebuild the book's rejected version. */
.table-rule       { fill: none; stroke: var(--table-rule); stroke-width: var(--table-rule-width); }
.table-rule-total { fill: none; stroke: var(--table-rule-total); stroke-width: var(--table-rule-width); }
.table-fill       { fill: var(--table-fill); stroke: none; }

.chart .cell, .chart .cell-bar, .legend-swatch { stroke: none; }
.chart .cell.good, .chart .cell.bad, .chart .legend-swatch.good, .chart .legend-swatch.bad { stroke: none; }
.cell-bar         { fill: var(--cell-bar); }
.cell-dot         { fill: var(--single); stroke-width: 0; }
/* a row of what is not known (role missing, G4.15): its dots in the missing grey, its bars (under their
   numbers) the grey paled, so that the text grey keeps 4.5 : 1 on them (G6.5) */
.cell-dot.missing { fill: var(--missing); }

.cvd-safe .good.div-m2, .cvd-safe .good.div-p2 { fill: var(--good-cvd-2); }
.cvd-safe .good.div-m3, .cvd-safe .good.div-p3 { fill: var(--good-cvd-3); }
.cvd-safe .good.div-m4, .cvd-safe .good.div-p4 { fill: var(--good-cvd-4); }
.cvd-safe .bad.div-m1, .cvd-safe .bad.div-p1 { fill: var(--bad-cvd-1); }

.cvd-safe .bad.div-m4, .cvd-safe .bad.div-p4 { fill: var(--bad-cvd-4); }
/* A cell that carries its value: its step set light (--cell-l-k, --cell-chroma), the text grey legible on it. */
.labelled.seq-1 { fill: oklch-light(var(--seq-1), var(--cell-l-1), var(--cell-chroma)); }

.labelled.good.div-m2, .labelled.good.div-p2 { fill: oklch-light(var(--good-2), var(--cell-l-5), var(--cell-chroma)); }

.series-2.shade-dark  { fill: var(--series-2-strong); stroke: var(--series-2-strong); }
.series-3.shade-dark  { fill: var(--series-3-strong); stroke: var(--series-3-strong); }
.series-4.shade-dark  { fill: var(--series-4-strong); stroke: var(--series-4-strong); }
.series-5.shade-dark  { fill: var(--series-5-strong); stroke: var(--series-5-strong); }
.series-6.shade-dark  { fill: var(--series-6-strong); stroke: var(--series-6-strong); }
.group-rule.series-1, .group-rule.series-2, .group-rule.series-3, .group-rule.series-4,
.group-rule.series-5, .group-rule.series-6 { fill: none; stroke-width: var(--grid-width); }
.text-group-1 { fill: var(--series-1-text); }  .text-group-2 { fill: var(--series-2-text); }
.text-group-3 { fill: var(--series-3-text); }  .text-group-4 { fill: var(--series-4-text); }
.text-group-5 { fill: var(--series-5-text); }  .text-group-6 { fill: var(--series-6-text); }

/* ---- Totals stacked (phase 3; SPEC §6.14): stacked bars, waterfalls, stacked areas. ------------
   A stack's segments are flat bars parted by a thin gap in the page colour where they meet (a true
   gap, half from each: G7.32, R7-33, M ≈ 1.5-2 px, s. 0230, 0241); an area's bands touch (G7.32);
   a waterfall's connector is a hairline at each running total (s. 0237), darker than the gridlines
   as the book's (≈ #A9A9A9) and as the signed zero line. */
:root {
  --segment-gap: 0.1em;            /* M ≈ 1.5-2 px at the book's size, about 0.1 of its label size */
  --single-stack-width: 0.35;      /* M 0.17-0.38 (s. 0223, 0230, 0240): one stack's bar, a share of the
                                      plot's height (the plot as high as a chart the figure's width) */
  --connector: #a6a6a6;            /* M ≈ #A9A9A9 (s. 0237); the signed zero line's grey */
}
.chart .segment, .chart .area { stroke: none; }
.connector    { fill: none; stroke: var(--connector); stroke-width: var(--grid-width); }

/* The plain chart style without its data colours (SPEC §5): the book's plain
   look, flat on the page, labels in New Computer Modern at 10 pt (owner,
   30 Sep 2026), titles 1.2 times and bold. Values are tokens on :root; the
   role rules below use them through var(). chartgen flattens this file
   (imports inlined, em in points, var() replaced) before bake.py reads it.

   Order matters (bake.py takes, for each class of a label, the first rule
   that mentions it): tokens, text roles (.prose first, then single-class
   rules), non-data, slot paints, highlight and context paints, then the
   mark-kind rules, which reset what does not apply to a kind.

   Tagged M (measured in the book), N (the notes' proposal), O (ours). An em
   is --label-size, never a CSS em. */
/* @defs plain-defs.svg */

:root {
  /* typography */
  --label-size: 10;                /* owner: the diagrams' size, at the 368 pt text width */
  --title-size: 1.2em;             /* M 1.17–1.35; bold */
  --note-size: 0.8em;              /* M; italic; the floor of D-6 */
  --inset-text-size: 0.8em;        /* M 0.73–0.82 */
  --line-pitch: 1.25em;            /* M 1.25–1.3: wrapped labels, title lines */
  --text-pad: 0.15em;              /* O: padding of text boxes in the collision test */

  /* notes under the chart and their marks (SPEC §6.19; owner, 1 Oct 2026: tables and charts may carry
     footnotes); the marks' look is the owner's to choose, the alternatives in examples/review/r1-footnotes */
  --note-marks: letters;           /* O: the marks' sequence, numbered in reading order: letters (a, b, c),
                                      numerals (1, 2, 3) or symbols (*, †, ‡, §, ‖, ¶); letters, since a raised
                                      figure beside a number can read as an exponent */
  --note-mark-gap: 0.05em;         /* O: a mark's gap after the text it marks (the face's side bearing does most) */
  --note-mark-lift: 0;             /* O: a mark's x-height (letters, numerals; figure height for symbols) at the
                                      cap height of the text it marks, then raised this much more */
  --note-hang: 0.3em;              /* O: a note's mark to its text under the chart; its later lines indented to the
                                      text */
  --note-mark-size: var(--note-size);  /* O: the notes' size, 0.8em, the floor of G6.4 */
  --note-mark-slant: italic;       /* O: italic, as the notes (README: the chart's own notes are italic) */
  --note-mark-ink: var(--note);    /* O: the note grey (4.5 : 1); on a fill, the colour of the text it marks */
  --note-footer-marks: raised;     /* O: a note's own mark under the chart, raised as in the chart, or on the
                                      baseline (baseline) */
  --notes-gap: 1em;                /* O: the chart's lowest ink to the first note's cap tops */

  /* value scale and unit phrase (6.4) */
  --scale-gap: 0.9em;              /* M 0.9–1.0: label column's right edge to the plot */
  --unit-space: 0.333em;           /* O: the typeface's word space, number to phrase */
  --unit-gridline-gap: 0.6em;      /* M 0.5–0.7: phrase end to the top gridline's start */
  --unit-min-gridline: 0.15;       /* N: shortest top gridline, a share of the plot width */
  --unit-clearance: 0.3em;         /* N: padding of the phrase in the collision test */
  --scale-label-drop: 0.5em;       /* M: horizontal scale, plot bottom to the labels' cap tops */
  --unit-line-drop: 0.55em;        /* O: horizontal scale, label row to the unit line's cap top (a line pitch
                                      between baselines; M 0.3 looked cramped at 10 pt) */

  /* categories and time (6.3, 6.7) */
  --category-gap: 0.8em;           /* M 0.6–1.0: zero line to the cap tops of category labels */
  --category-label-gap: 0.6em;     /* M: horizontal bars, label right edge to the plot */
  --category-label-sep: 1em;       /* owner (30 Sep 2026): least clear space between neighbouring names
                                      under vertical bars, which may reach past their bands; the gap must
                                      read wider than the spaces inside a name */
  --time-row-pitch: 1.8em;         /* M ≈ 2: cap top to cap top between time rows */
  --time-label-sep: 0.6em;         /* N: thinning, least space between time labels */
  --divider-clear: 0.3em;          /* O (owner, 30 Sep 2026): least space between a time label and a
                                      divider, half the space between two labels; the outer dividers move
                                      out to keep it, a label beside an inner one keeps its place with a halo */
  --divider-halo: 0.6em;           /* O (owner, 1 Oct 2026): the halo's stroke round a label's letters, twice
                                      --divider-clear, so that it reaches the clearance outside them */

  /* title block (D-5: left-aligned, a descriptive line in the label style) */
  --title-gap: 1.6em;              /* O: last title baseline to the top scale line's baseline */
  --title-align: start;            /* D-5 (a): left, flush with the scale labels */
  --title-align-insight: start;

  /* plot and bars */
  --plot-aspect: 0.6;              /* M ≈ 0.64; O: plot height / plot width */
  --bar-row-pitch: 2em;            /* O: band of horizontal bars when the height is free */
  --band-fill: 0.556;              /* M 0.55–0.56: bar : gap = 5 : 4 (R9-8, D-35) */
  --cluster-fill: 0.714;           /* M 0.72 (phase 2) */
  --cluster-inner-gap: 0;          /* M: bars of a cluster touch */
  --cluster-min-gap: 1;            /* G7.5s: clusters at least one bar width apart (M 1.0 with 2–3 series, s. 0307,
                                      0319; 2.25 with six, s. 0331: the cluster fill gives 2.4) (phase 2) */
  --target-mark: 0.2;              /* G7.57s: a flat reference marker's thickness, in bar widths (M s. 0321) */
  --target-mark-max: 0.4em;        /* M ≈ 0.36–0.4em (s. 0148, s. 0321): no thicker, however wide the bars */
  --value-label-gap: 0.3em;        /* O: a value label's gap to its bar's end (G7.4) (phase 2) */
  --table-gap: 2em;                /* M ≈ 2em (s. 0307): the last category row's baseline to a companion
                                      table's first row (phase 2) */
  --table-row-pitch: 1.6em;        /* M ≈ 1.65em (s. 0307): a companion table's rows (G7.39s gives 2.15em for
                                      a table alone) */
  --table-col-gap: 1.5em;          /* G7.39s: between a table's columns, and between the bars and a table beside
                                      them */
  --table-header-drop: 0.75em;     /* O: a table beside horizontal bars, its headers' baseline above the plot */
  --key-gap: 0.25em;               /* O: a table row's key square to its name (the legend's --legend-gap) */
  --key-tint: 0.6;                 /* O: a row's pill or halo, its series colour this far towards the page (the
                                      least at which the text grey keeps 4.5 : 1 on all of slots 1-3: 4.68 on the
                                      orange) */
  --key-pill-pad-x: 0.35em;        /* O: a pill's room either side of its name */
  --key-pill-pad-y: 0.2em;         /* O: and above and below the name's capitals (plus 1 pt) */
  --key-halo-width: 0.3em;         /* O: a halo's stroke round the letters (half of it shows outside them) */
  --missing-note-lift: 0.3em;      /* O: note baseline above the zero line */
  --missing-note-inset: 0.3em;     /* O: horizontal bars, zero line to the note */

  /* lines, dots and end labels (later stages) */
  --line-width: 0.2em;             /* M 0.15–0.23em */
  --line-width-highlight: 0.4em;   /* M × 2 (06) */
  --marker-size: 0.4em;            /* M: diameter, twice the line */
  --dot-size: 0.5em;               /* M: a time dot plot's filled dot (s. 0163) */
  --category-dot-size: 0.75em;     /* M: a categorical dot plot's open circle, centre-line diameter (outside
                                      ≈ 0.85em with its ring; s. 0082, 0085) */
  --dot-ring: 0.3;                 /* M: the open circle's ring in units of its radius (≈ 1.1 pt; s. 0085) */
  --end-label-gap: 0.5em;          /* M 0.3–0.9 */
  --end-label-pitch: 1.25em;       /* M */
  --end-label-max-shift: 1;        /* N: pitches, then a legend */
  --end-label-leader-shift: 1.5;   /* D-7: pitches a label may move with a leader to its line */
  --leader-run: 1em;               /* O: how much further right a label with a leader sits */
  --legend-margin: 1em;            /* O: plot edge to a legend column at its right (lines) */

  /* time charts of phase 2: thin bars, true time axes, arrows, symbols */
  --event-bar-width: 0.28em;       /* D-42: a thin bar 1.2–1.5 × the line width (1.4 ×); M ≈ 1.2–1.5 × (s. 0181) */
  --time-tick: 0.45em;             /* D-45 (ii): a true time axis's tick at a boundary of its labelled unit */
  --time-tick-minor: 0.25em;       /* D-45 (ii): a tick at each day (or month) of the data's grain */
  --arrow-head-length: 0.65em;     /* notes 06 §5.4: about 3 × the line width; the tip on the after value */
  --arrow-head-width: 0.55em;      /* about 2.5 × the line width */
  --arrow-start-size: 0.5em;       /* the dot at the before value, about 2.2 × the line width (diameter) */
  --arrow-panel-gap: 2em;          /* O: between an arrow chart's absolute and % panels */
  --arrow-short-head: fit;         /* O (owner to judge, review r1-arrows): a change shorter than a full head
                                      beside its dot: fit (the head shrinks to the room, to half size, then
                                      overhangs the dot, haloed), overhang, head-only, or hidden (the former) */
  --arrow-head-halo: 0.12em;       /* O: the page-coloured outline round a head drawn over its start dot */
  --symbol-size: 0.55em;           /* R6-30: a black-and-white marker symbol, M ≈ 0.5em (s. 0200) */

  /* insets (6.6) */
  --inset-frame-width: 1.5;        /* M 2.5–4 × the gridline: frames and links */
  --inset-radius: 6;               /* M ≈ 1.8 % of the chart width */
  --inset-pad-x: 0.3;              /* N: bands, source frame round its marks, across them */
  --inset-pad-y: 0.4em;            /* N: source frame round its marks, along them; round a band */
  --inset-margin: 0.6em;           /* O: frame to inset content; a band's source frame inside the inset's */
  --inset-gap: 1.5em;              /* O: between a band inset's frame and its source frame, where the links run
                                      (M ≈ 1.6em, s. 0081, s. 0297) */
  --inset-fade: 0.85;              /* M: bar widths faded below the lowest inset gridline (s. 0297) */
  --inset-height-ratio: 0.8;       /* M: narrow-range inset plot / main plot */
  --inset-max-height: 1;           /* owner (30 Sep 2026): an inset's plot at most about as high as its main
                                      chart's (above or below it) */
  --inset-share-height: 0.9;       /* O: an aligned inset shares its main chart's axis when, labelled twice,
                                      the figure would be taller than this × its width (D-56) */

  /* small multiples and merged charts (phase 2, 6.10) */
  --panel-gap: 0.8em;              /* O: least space between the texts of neighbouring panels (merged bars:
                                      M about one band, notes 02 §5.3); a separator runs in its middle */
  --panel-min-height: 3em;         /* O: a panel's plot at least this high, three intervals one em apart, so
                                      that a stack of twelve fits a page (the book's stacks ≈ 3.5–4em, s. 0203) */
  --panel-max-aspect: 1.5;         /* O: a panel's plot at most this × its width high (the book's rows of
                                      panels, s. 0339–0340, stand 1.5–1.8 × as high as wide) */

  /* legends (phase 2) */
  --legend-key: 0.55em;            /* M: square key; a line key is 2em */
  --legend-line-key: 2em;
  --legend-gap: 0.25em;            /* M: key to text */
  --legend-entry-gap: 1em;         /* M: between entries */

  /* one total's breakdown (phase 3): pies, treemaps, wrapped bars */
  --pie-radius: 0.2;               /* O: the pie's radius, a share of the figure's width (M ≈ 0.18-0.19 of the
                                      book's column, s. 0265), smaller when its labels need the room */
  --pie-min-radius: 3em;           /* O: no smaller; a pie whose labels will not fit round it then is refused */
  --pie-gap: 0.007;                /* G7.26s, M: the gap between slices, a share of the diameter (a true gap:
                                      each slice's straight edges moved in by half of it) */
  --pie-label-gap: 0.1;            /* N (07 §5.2): the rim to a label's nearest point, a share of the radius */
  --pie-label-width: 7em;          /* O: a slice's name wider than this wraps onto two lines (s. 0222) */
  --pie-leader-angle: 8;           /* D-34, N: a slice under this many degrees gets a leader (G7.29) */
  --donut-hole: 0.74;              /* M (s. 0269): a donut's hole, a share of its radius (only through an
                                      override of R7-39) */
  --tile-gap: 1;                   /* M 1 px: the page between neighbouring tiles of a treemap (G7.34) */
  --tile-group-gap: 2.5;           /* M 1-2 px at the book's size: between the groups of a treemap */
  --tile-pad: 0.3em;               /* M ≈ 3 px: a tile's label inset from its lower left corner */
  --tile-min-chars: 3;             /* O: a name cut short keeps at least this many letters before "…" */
  --wrap-max-aspect: 1.2;          /* O: a wrapped bar chart's columns at most this × the figure's width high;
                                      the fewest columns that keep within it (G7.7) */
  --wrap-column-gap: 1.5em;        /* O: between a column's scale labels and the next column's names */

  /* greys and lines (5.3) */
  --grid-width: 0.6;               /* O: the diagrams' hairline (M ≈ 0.72 at this size) */
  --page: #ffffff;
  --text: #595959;                 /* M; contrast 7.0 */
  --note: #767676;                 /* O: 4.5 : 1 (D-6), not the book's ≈ #B0B0B0 */
  --grid: #d9d9d9;                 /* M; contrast 1.41 */
  --zero-line: #d9d9d9;            /* M: the zero line is a gridline (R1-07) */
  --zero-line-signed: #a6a6a6;     /* M: darker only inside a signed range (D-17) */
  --divider: #d9d9d9;
  --inset-frame: #d9d9d9;
  --projection-dash: 0 5;          /* M: dots one line wide */
  --projection-dash-highlight: 0 10;  /* O: the same dots on a line twice as thick */
  --leader: #bfbfbf;               /* M: the book's leader grey (pie leaders #C0C0C0, 5.5) */
  --uniform-context: #bfbfbf;      /* M: only for rebuilding the rejected grey-out (R6-28) */
  --comment: #3f63b0;              /* N (phase 2) */
  --link: #bfbfbf;                 /* M (phase 2) */
  --tile-text: #1a1a1a;            /* O (phase 3): a treemap tile's label, at least 4.5 : 1 on every first-tier
                                      colour and the sixth (4.7 on the purple; the text grey is 3.3 on the blue,
                                      and the book's white on its #558BB9 is 3.6) */
}

/* ---- Text. Every label is <text class="prose modifiers… role">. ---------- */
.prose        { font-family: NewComputerModern, "New Computer Modern"; font-size: var(--label-size);
                fill: var(--text); }
.title        { font-size: var(--title-size); font-weight: bold; }
.missing-note { font-size: var(--note-size); font-style: italic; fill: var(--note); }
.incomplete-note { font-size: var(--note-size); font-style: italic; fill: var(--note); }  /* "As of Dec. 10" */
.arrow-key    { font-size: var(--note-size); fill: var(--note); }  /* G7.21s: the arrow key; upright, italic is the comments' (owner, 30 Sep 2026) */
.inset-text   { font-size: var(--inset-text-size); }
.text-strong  { font-weight: bold; }
.panel-title  { font-weight: bold; }   /* a merged chart's panel heading (G7.6: bold, M s. 0067, 0363) */
.tile-label   { fill: var(--tile-text); }   /* a treemap's names, inside their tiles (phase 3) */
.chart-note   { font-size: var(--note-size); font-style: italic; fill: var(--note); }  /* the chart's own note
                                                 under it: a treemap's parts too small to name (phase 3) */
.footnote     { font-size: var(--note-size); font-style: italic; fill: var(--note); }  /* a note under the chart
                                                 referred to by its mark (SPEC §6.19); a plain note is a chart-note */
.note-mark    { font-size: var(--note-mark-size); font-style: var(--note-mark-slant); fill: var(--note-mark-ink); }
                                              /* a note's mark, raised,
                                                 after what it explains and before the note (SPEC §6.19) */
.on-fill      { fill: var(--text); }   /* a note's mark on a filled cell or tile, after the classes of the text it
                                          marks: in that text's colour, never the note grey (SPEC §6.19) */

/* ---- Non-data: light and thin, under the marks (R1-02, R1-09). ------------ */
.gridline             { fill: none; stroke: var(--grid); stroke-width: var(--grid-width); }
.gridline.zero        { stroke: var(--zero-line); }
.gridline.zero.signed { stroke: var(--zero-line-signed); }
.time-divider         { fill: none; stroke: var(--divider); stroke-width: var(--grid-width); }
.panel-divider        { fill: none; stroke: var(--divider); stroke-width: var(--grid-width); }  /* G7.51 */
.inset-frame         { fill: var(--page); stroke: var(--inset-frame); stroke-width: var(--inset-frame-width); }
.inset-source, .inset-link { fill: none; stroke: var(--inset-frame); stroke-width: var(--inset-frame-width); }

/* ---- Data colours by slot or role (tokens in the palette file). ------------ */
.single     { fill: var(--single); stroke: var(--single); }
.series-1   { fill: var(--series-1); stroke: var(--series-1); }
.series-2   { fill: var(--series-2); stroke: var(--series-2); }
.series-3   { fill: var(--series-3); stroke: var(--series-3); }
.series-4   { fill: var(--series-4); stroke: var(--series-4); }
.series-5   { fill: var(--series-5); stroke: var(--series-5); }
.series-6   { fill: var(--series-6); stroke: var(--series-6); }
.series-7   { fill: var(--series-7); stroke: var(--series-7); }
.series-8   { fill: var(--series-8); stroke: var(--series-8); }
.series-9   { fill: var(--series-9); stroke: var(--series-9); }
.series-10  { fill: var(--series-10); stroke: var(--series-10); }
.series-11  { fill: var(--series-11); stroke: var(--series-11); }
.series-12  { fill: var(--series-12); stroke: var(--series-12); }
.series-13  { fill: var(--series-13); stroke: var(--series-13); }
.series-14  { fill: var(--series-14); stroke: var(--series-14); }
.series-15  { fill: var(--series-15); stroke: var(--series-15); }
.series-16  { fill: var(--series-16); stroke: var(--series-16); }
.average    { fill: var(--average); stroke: var(--average); }
.total      { fill: var(--total); stroke: var(--total); }
.all-others { fill: var(--all-others); stroke: var(--all-others); }
.reference  { fill: var(--reference-line); stroke: var(--reference-line); }
.missing    { fill: var(--missing); stroke: var(--missing); }
.good       { fill: var(--good); stroke: var(--good); }
.bad        { fill: var(--bad); stroke: var(--bad); }

/* ---- Highlight: the same hue, stronger (R3-7, R15-6, 6.9). ----------------- */
.single.highlight     { fill: var(--single-strong); stroke: var(--single-strong); }
.series-1.highlight   { fill: var(--series-1-strong); stroke: var(--series-1-strong); }
.series-2.highlight   { fill: var(--series-2-strong); stroke: var(--series-2-strong); }
.series-3.highlight   { fill: var(--series-3-strong); stroke: var(--series-3-strong); }
.series-4.highlight   { fill: var(--series-4-strong); stroke: var(--series-4-strong); }
.series-5.highlight   { fill: var(--series-5-strong); stroke: var(--series-5-strong); }

/* ---- Mark kinds: flat, no outlines (R1-03). --------------------------------- */

                stroke-linejoin: round; stroke-linecap: round; }

/* Time charts of phase 2. A step line keeps square corners and stops exactly at the as-of
   date (notes 06 §5.4); a thin bar is flat like a bar; a true time axis has short ticks in the
   divider grey (D-45 (ii)); an arrow's shaft is a line, its head and start dot filled; the
   level mark of an incomplete period is dotted like a projection (02 D10). */
.step-line.single, .incomplete-mark.single       { stroke: var(--single-line); }

   the letters by the clearance instead of crossing them (flat: no card, no shadow). */

                    stroke-linejoin: round; }

/* Several series over categories (phase 2). A bar's legend key is a small filled square, a
   dot's the dot itself, open or filled as the chart's dots are (G5.14); a flat reference
   marker across a bar, and its key, in the strong shade of the bar's hue (R11-4, G7.57), else

.target-mark.series-4, .target-key.series-4 { fill: var(--series-4-strong); }

/* A table's row keys (table.row_key; phase 2, for the owner's choice): a name in its series'
   strong shade (text-*), a pale tint of the series behind the name (a pill) or round its letters
   (a flat halo: a copy of the name, text-halo, filled and stroked in the tint under the name). */

/* ---- Tables alone, heatmaps, ramps and their keys (phase 3; SPEC §6.14–§6.16). ------------ */
:root {
  /* a table alone (R10-12–R10-25; G7.37–G7.45; D-52) */
  --table-alone-pitch: 2.15em;     /* G7.39s, M ≈ 2.15em (s. 0315): rows set well apart, no stripes */
  --table-total-gap: 3em;          /* G7.39s, M ≈ 3em: the gutter before a Total column (1.5em elsewhere,
                                      --table-col-gap) */
  --table-rule-width: 0.6;         /* M 1 px: the rule under the header and the one above the totals */
  --table-rule-drop: 0.6em;        /* O: the header's baseline to its rule */
  --table-fill-pad: 0.35em;        /* O: a highlighted cell's fill beyond its text, each side (M s. 0317) */
  --table-fill-inset: 0.2em;       /* O: a fill's top and bottom inside its row's pitch (M ≈ 1.8 of 2.15em) */
  --table-rule: #a3a3a3;           /* M s. 0317 (D-52 (iii)): under the header, mid grey */
  --table-rule-total: #656565;     /* M s. 0317: above the totals, darker */
  --table-fill: #e8e8e8;           /* G7.44s, M s. 0317: the few cells that matter */
  /* heatmaps (R6-36, R12-6; G7.35, G7.36) */
  --cell-pitch: 1.6em;             /* M ≈ 1.7em (s. 0329, s. 0309): the rows of a heatmap table or a shaded
                                      table; the cells touch */
  --heat-row-pitch: 1em;           /* O: a heatmap of many series, a row each: its names at the label size (the
                                      layout widens it when names with descenders would meet; the book's names
                                      are tiny, s. 0204) */
  --summary-gap: 0.4em;            /* M ≈ 0.3 row (s. 0329): a summary row (Overall Avg.) set apart */
  --heat-max-column: 5em;          /* O: a heatmap table's columns at most this wide (cells of the widest value
                                      and heading otherwise) */
  /* a ramp's key (G5.13, R4-9): a graduated bar, its title above, its values below */
  --ramp-key-width: 12em;          /* O (M ≈ 14em × 1.3em at the book's size, 03-04 §5.4) */
  --ramp-key-height: 0.7em;
  --ramp-key-gap: 0.35em;          /* O: the title to the bar, the bar to its values */
  --key-tick: 0.3em;               /* O: the mark at a diverging key's dividing value */
  /* in-table graphics (R10-9, G7.47) */
  --cell-bar-height: 0.9em;        /* O: a bar under its cell's number (M ≈ 0.6 of the row, s. 0309) */
  --cell-dot: 0.55em;              /* O: a dot in its cell's strip */
  --cell-strip: 3em;               /* O: the strip of dots beside a column's numbers */
  --sparkline-width: 0.12em;       /* M ≈ 1.5 px (s. 0309) */
  --trend-width: 4em;              /* O: the Trend column's sparklines */
  /* action dots (R12-4, G7.58) */
  --action-pitch: 2em;             /* M ≈ 2.3em (s. 0327) */
  --action-bar: 0.35;              /* M: the bar's thickness, a share of the row's pitch */
  --action-bar-length: 8em;        /* O: the longest bar */
  --action-dot: 0.75em;            /* M ≈ 0.9 × the text's height (s. 0327) */
  --action-gap: 0.6em;             /* O: between the name, the bar, the value and the dot */
  /* values printed in strong cells (owner, 1 Oct 2026; a muted cell, chart.cells, is the spec's):
     contrast (the owner's choice: each value black or white, whichever has more contrast on its
     cell) or plate (the value in the text grey on a plate of the step's pale version, kept for
     comparison); ramps.CELL_VALUE_MODES */
  --cell-values: contrast;
  --cell-text-dark: #000000;       /* O: on a mid cell only black keeps 4.5 : 1 (4.68 on --seq-7; #1a1a1a 3.88) */
  --cell-text-light: #ffffff;
  --cell-plate-pad: 0.2em;         /* O: a plate's margin round a value's ink */
  /* censored values in a heatmap ("<1" below a detection limit, ">2,420" above a range; SPEC §6.15), a
     state of their own, never the missing grey: step (a step of the ramp of their own below its lowest
     class, its own entry in the key), printed (the palest class's colour, "<1" printed in the cell),
     pale (a pale fill of their own), hatch or dots (the page under a fine hatch or dots). The owner's
     choice to make (examples/review/r1-below-limit); step provisionally. */
  --censored-cells: step;
  --censored: #e4e0da;             /* O: pale, lighter than the missing grey (#a6a6a6), apart from the page */
  --censored-mark: #8c8c8c;        /* O: the hatch's lines and the dots, on the page's white */
  --censored-hatch-gap: 0.25em;
  --censored-dot: 0.09em;
}

.chart .censored-hatched, .chart .censored-dotted, .legend-swatch.censored-hatched,

.cvd-safe .labelled.bad.div-m1, .cvd-safe .labelled.bad.div-p1 { fill: oklch-light(var(--bad-cvd-1), var(--cell-l-3), var(--cell-chroma)); }
.cvd-safe .labelled.bad.div-m2, .cvd-safe .labelled.bad.div-p2 { fill: oklch-light(var(--bad-cvd-2), var(--cell-l-5), var(--cell-chroma)); }
.cvd-safe .labelled.bad.div-m3, .cvd-safe .labelled.bad.div-p3 { fill: oklch-light(var(--bad-cvd-3), var(--cell-l-7), var(--cell-chroma)); }
.cvd-safe .labelled.bad.div-m4, .cvd-safe .labelled.bad.div-p4 { fill: oklch-light(var(--bad-cvd-4), var(--cell-l-9), var(--cell-chroma)); }
/* A value on a strong cell (--cell-values): the dark or the light tone, or a plate (cell-plate, with
   the step's labelled classes, so its fill is the step's pale version). */
.on-mid-cell  { fill: var(--cell-text-dark); }
.on-dark-cell { fill: var(--cell-text-light); }
.chart .cell-plate { stroke: none; }
/* Grouped shades (G4.9; D-49): a group's members in its hue, light, base (no class) and strong;
   the group's name in the hue dark enough for text (G5.12; upright, the owner's rule for keys). */
.series-1.shade-light { fill: var(--series-1-shade-light); stroke: var(--series-1-shade-light); }
.series-2.shade-light { fill: var(--series-2-shade-light); stroke: var(--series-2-shade-light); }
.series-3.shade-light { fill: var(--series-3-shade-light); stroke: var(--series-3-shade-light); }
.series-4.shade-light { fill: var(--series-4-shade-light); stroke: var(--series-4-shade-light); }
.series-5.shade-light { fill: var(--series-5-shade-light); stroke: var(--series-5-shade-light); }
.series-6.shade-light { fill: var(--series-6-shade-light); stroke: var(--series-6-shade-light); }
.series-1.shade-dark  { fill: var(--series-1-strong); stroke: var(--series-1-strong); }
.series-2.shade-dark  { fill: var(--series-2-strong); stroke: var(--series-2-strong); }
.series-3.shade-dark  { fill: var(--series-3-strong); stroke: var(--series-3-strong); }
.series-4.shade-dark  { fill: var(--series-4-strong); stroke: var(--series-4-strong); }
.series-5.shade-dark  { fill: var(--series-5-strong); stroke: var(--series-5-strong); }
.series-6.shade-dark  { fill: var(--series-6-strong); stroke: var(--series-6-strong); }
.group-rule.series-1, .group-rule.series-2, .group-rule.series-3, .group-rule.series-4,
.group-rule.series-5, .group-rule.series-6 { fill: none; stroke-width: var(--grid-width); }
.text-group-1 { fill: var(--series-1-text); }  .text-group-2 { fill: var(--series-2-text); }
.text-group-3 { fill: var(--series-3-text); }  .text-group-4 { fill: var(--series-4-text); }
.text-group-5 { fill: var(--series-5-text); }  .text-group-6 { fill: var(--series-6-text); }

/* ---- Totals stacked (phase 3; SPEC §6.14): stacked bars, waterfalls, stacked areas. ------------
   A stack's segments are flat bars parted by a thin gap in the page colour where they meet (a true
   gap, half from each: G7.32, R7-33, M ≈ 1.5-2 px, s. 0230, 0241); an area's bands touch (G7.32);
   a waterfall's connector is a hairline at each running total (s. 0237), darker than the gridlines
   as the book's (≈ #A9A9A9) and as the signed zero line. */
:root {
  --segment-gap: 0.1em;            /* M ≈ 1.5-2 px at the book's size, about 0.1 of its label size */
  --single-stack-width: 0.35;      /* M 0.17-0.38 (s. 0223, 0230, 0240): one stack's bar, a share of the
                                      plot's height (the plot as high as a chart the figure's width) */
  --connector: #a6a6a6;            /* M ≈ #A9A9A9 (s. 0237); the signed zero line's grey */
}
.chart .segment, .chart .area { stroke: none; }
.connector    { fill: none; stroke: var(--connector); stroke-width: var(--grid-width); }
